change.title: pr-40940-flat
change.description: Fix concurrent group access to prevent NullPointerException
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined and never stopped if a delete fails
findings.body:
The reader thread is started on line 139 and never joined. `deletedAll.set(true)` on line 155 is not in a `finally`. Two problems follow.

1. If any `remove()` on line 153 throws, `deletedAll` is never set. The thread then loops forever, sending requests to the shared admin client, and the test failure surfaces while that thread is still running against the realm that is being torn down.
2. On the passing path, `assertThat` on line 157 runs right after the flag is set. The thread can still be inside a `groups()` call, and any exception from that call lands in `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has already passed. The last read, which is the one that runs after the final delete, is not checked.

Fix: wrap the delete loop in `try/finally` that sets the flag, call `join()` on the thread, then assert. Using an `ExecutorService` or `CompletableFuture` would also work.

findings.title: Test does not reliably reproduce or pin the race it targets
findings.body: The reader runs a single `groups(null, 0, MAX, true)` call per iteration, with no coordination with the deletes, so whether a group disappears between listing and `getSubGroupsCount()` is down to timing. The test can pass without the fix. It also does not check which exception was caught, so a failure is reported only as a list of unrelated exceptions. Consider asserting that at least one read ran, and having the reader skip nothing silently. Failing with the first caught exception as the cause would make diagnosis easier. The name `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` and the `groupUuuids` typo (three u's) are also worth tidying. Line 117 is a whitespace-only line.

findings.title: Null-guard added only to getSubGroupsCount; the sibling delegations still NPE for a deleted group
findings.body:
`getSubGroupsCount()` now tolerates `modelSupplier.get()` returning null, which happens when the group was deleted after the adapter was created (`getGroupModel()` at line 299 returns null from `getGroupById`). The three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 call `modelSupplier.get().…` with no check. A concurrent delete hits them with the same NPE. Decide whether those should also return an empty stream, or document why only the count needs the guard.

The null return is also silent. `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/GroupUtils.java:90) passes it straight to `setSubGroupCount`, so a group deleted mid-request is still listed, now with a null `subGroupCount`. A missing count is probably acceptable, but it is worth knowing that the response can contain a group that no longer exists.

findings.title: Removal of unused private method is safe
findings.body: `groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement` was private, and a grep of the repository found no remaining references. The remaining imports are still all used.

contracts.action: GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount now tolerates a missing backing group by returning null instead of throwing NPE
contracts.equivalent_path: Sibling delegations getSubGroupsStream(...) at GroupAdapter.java:254-269 also go through modelSupplier.get() when the adapter is not updated, and do not null-check.
contracts.before_after: Before: getGroupModel() was called directly and dereferenced, so a deleted group gave an NPE. After: the lazy supplier is used and a null model gives a null count. The sibling stream methods still dereference without a check.
contracts.visible_effect: GET /groups with subGroupsCount=true (the default) used to fail with a 500 when a group was deleted between listing and counting. It now returns the group with a null subGroupCount (GroupUtils.java:90, GroupsResource.java:113-124).
contracts.failure_mode: Silent: the deleted group stays in the response with a null count. The stream overloads still NPE in the same race.

contracts.action: New concurrency test starts a reader thread against the groups list endpoint while groups are deleted
contracts.failure_mode: The thread is not joined and not stopped if a delete throws. It can leak and loop forever, and late exceptions can be missed by the assertion.

summary: The `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount` null-guard fixes the NPE when a group is deleted mid-listing. The three `getSubGroupsStream` overloads still dereference the same supplier without a check. The new test has a lifecycle defect: its reader thread is never joined and is not stopped if a delete throws, so late exceptions can slip past the assertion and a failed delete leaves the thread looping. The `CachedGroup` `@Override` and the removal of the unused private method in `GroupUtils` are fine.
